newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares await Dow, rally seen.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares await Dow, rally seen.

text.p: Leading Russian shares opened firmer on Wednesday but eased later on light volumes, traders said, forecasting continuing sensitivity to movements on Wall Street.
But a slight rally is possible toward the end of the week, they said.
"There is practically no movement on the market this morning. Everyone is waiting for the opening of the U.S. markets," said Yuri Agaronik, head of analysis at Prospekt brokerage.
The Russian Trading System index of 23 shares opened at 298.36, down from the previous close of 298.52.
Oil producer Purneftegaz PFGS.RTS was down slightly at $5.05 at 0915 GMT after $5.18 on Tuesday and national power utility UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.1896 from $0.1875.
"We've seen the Russian market has been influenced by foreign markets since the end of last year. That influence is going to increase," said senior trader at Rossiisky Kredit Bank Nikolai Chikhachev.
But he said that day to day movements on the Dow Jones index would not be reflected on the RTS.

"In the long term there is a dependency in that when there are big movements in the West, investors pay less attention to Russia, but that's not reaction that happens in one day," said Igor Rojkov of Credit Suisse.
Dealers said despite a continuing downward trend, a technical rise in the market index was possible towards the end of the week to balance the fall on Tuesday.
"The index has been hovering around 300 for the last few days and if it hits 300 today I think we will see a rally towards the end of the week," said Chikhachev.

He said a combination of new funds and a fall in yields from government securities pushing Russian banks into the market would contribute to a slight price spurt among leading shares in the near future.
